items: The CEC does not hold office during the pleasure of the President, despite being appointed by the President.
Other Election Commissioners can be removed by the President only on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
A key constitutional flaw frequently tested is that the Constitution has not debarred retiring Election Commissioners from further government appointments.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 324 provides constitutional safeguards to ensure the independent and impartial functioning of the Election Commission.
The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) is provided with security of tenure and cannot be removed except in the same manner and on the same grounds as a judge of the Supreme Court.
The service conditions of the Chief Election Commissioner cannot be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.
Other Election Commissioners or Regional Commissioners cannot be removed from office except on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
The Constitution has not prescribed qualifications (legal, educational, administrative) for members nor debarred retiring commissioners from further government appointments.
